title: 1.4 · Counting and remembering (Variables)
name: Counting and remembering (Variables)
summary: Students use a variable, a labeled box the program can look in and change, to count gems so a door opens. In Robo Route the watch pill shows what is in the box as the program runs; set puts a number in, change by adds to it, and a countdown level runs the box down to zero. Pairs share one device.
iCan: use a variable (a labeled box) to count things as the program runs
tell the difference between set and change by
say what is in the box at any moment of the run
materials: Variable Jars printable (jar labels, counters, set and change cards)
doNow: Think of the score in your favorite game. What makes it go up? What makes it go down? Write one of each.
plan: Explore: the count box and the watch pill on level 1

warmup.why: two retrieval items from 1.3, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from 1.3

do: Open Robo Route at Variables on the projector (Open game at this chapter). Level 1 has five gems up the left side and a door next to the flag that opens only when the count box says 5. Build it with the class: set count to 0, then repeat 5 with forward, pick up, change count by 1 inside, then turn right, forward, forward. Point at the watch pill before you press Run.
Press Step instead of Run. After each pick-up, stop and read the watch pill out loud with the class: 1, 2, 3. At the door, say what the box holds and watch it open.
say: A variable is a labeled box the program can look in and change. The label is its name; the number inside is its value.
Set empties the box and puts a new number in. Change by adds to what is already there. The watch pill shows the box right now.
ask: What is in the box right now?
explore.afterAsk: Ask it three times during the step-through, at different moments. Then ask what would happen if we forgot set count to 0 at the start, and try it: the box keeps the old number.
explore.bigIdea: A variable is a labeled box the program can look in and change while it runs.

play.stretch: the chapter, then 3 stars; level 5 keeps two boxes at once
play.pairs: driver and navigator on one device; the Swap! banner shows every 3 levels; the navigator watches the pill and calls out the value after every block
lookFors: set where change by was needed: the box empties and refills to 1 every time instead of counting up
no set count to 0 at the start, so the box carries an old number into the run
on the random levels (2 and 6), change count by 1 outside the if, so Bolt counts squares instead of gems
play.misconception: Change count by 1 does not put 1 in the box: it adds 1 to what is already there; set is the block that puts a number in.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

discuss: What did the box hold at the end of level 2? Show the watch pill and say how it got there.
Level 3 counted down to 0 instead of up. When is counting down the better choice: lives, a timer, steps left?
showMe: One pair runs level 5 on the projector in step mode; the class calls out both boxes, gems and turns, after every block.

exit.sentencePrompt: What is a variable like, and why does a program need one?

rubric.line: Variables: what a variable is and how a program changes it
levels: Says a variable holds a number or is a box, with nothing about changing it
Says a variable is a named box the program can look in and change, with an example: count, lives, score
Also tells set from change by, or says what the box held at the end of a level and why

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: the watch pill is always on; the navigator reads it after every block
hint 1 reminds the pair to set the box to 0 first; read-aloud on
levels 1 and 3 give the repeat count, so the only new idea is the box
stretch: level 5 with two boxes, then say what each box is for in one sentence each
invent a third thing to count on level 6 and say which block would change it

unpluggedTwin.title: Variable Jars
materials: two jars per group with blank labels
set and change cards (set gems to 0, change gems by 2, change lives by -1, set lives to 3)
steps: Label one jar gems and one jar lives. One partner is the program and reads cards one at a time; the other is the computer and does exactly what the card says to the jar: set empties it and puts in that many counters; change by adds or takes away.
After every card, a third partner (or the whole group) says the value out loud: what is in the jar right now? Write the two values on a strip after each card, like a watch pill.
Trick round: shuffle in a set card in the middle. Watch the jar empty and refill. Ask: what did set do that change by never does?
Share: which jar reached zero first? What card would you add to make the program fair?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: think of the score in your favorite game and write one thing that makes it go up and one that makes it go down.

Play Robo Route, chapter Variables, in pairs for 20 minutes. Classes, then the lesson, then Play. If the game asks, the quest code is 4 1 0 0. Goal: 4 levels. No warm-up and no projector needed; sign in with the login cards so the work is saved (signed out is fine only if the cards are missing). No devices or no internet? Run the unplugged twin printed below (Variable Jars, 15 minutes), then talk about the two discussion questions for 5 minutes.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

shortPeriod40.discuss: What did the box hold at the end of level 2? Show the watch pill and say how it got there.
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut; in 5 minutes of Explore run level 1 once with Run and once with Step, nothing more

add: the Variable Jars twin (15 minutes) before Play
the 3-star stretch and the two-box level after Play
10 minutes of the Unit 1 review on Brain Board

notes: Set versus change by is the whole lesson: when a pair is stuck, ask them to read the watch pill after each block and say which block moved it.
Level 4 counts bumps with a when block: the event from 1.3 changes the box, which surprises some pairs in a good way.
Shared devices: this is an even lesson, so partner B signs in; the gradebook and the Standards tab count the signed-in student.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: Think of the score in your favorite game. What makes it go up? What makes it go down? Write one of each.

Big idea: A variable is a labeled box the program can look in and change while it runs.

We will talk about:
- What did the box hold at the end of level 2? How did it get there?
- Level 3 counted down instead of up. When is counting down the better choice?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Play: Variables
steps.body:
Goal: 4 levels. Stretch: finish the chapter, then 3 stars.
If the game asks for a quest code, it is 4 1 0 0.
Pairs: driver and navigator. Swap when the Swap! banner shows. The navigator watches the pill and calls out the number after every block.
Set puts a number in the box. Change by adds to it. Start with set count to 0.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about variables, set and change by.
